title: Ligurian Republic
capsule: The Ligurian Republic was a French client state established on 14 June 1797 when Napoleon's Italian campaign supplanted the ancient Republic of Genoa, adopting the motto Libertà, Eguaglianza and a directorial constitution modelled on France. A revised Napoleonic constitution of 1802 restored a Doge as president of a Senate, reverting toward Genoese tradition. Austrian and British forces besieged Genoa in 1800, causing approximately 30,000 casualties, before French control was reestablished. Napoleon annexed the republic directly to the First French Empire as three départements in June 1805; the Congress of Vienna in 1815 transferred Liguria to Piedmont-Sardinia as the Duchy of Genoa.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is clearly documented; the republic corresponded closely to the former Republic of Genoa's jurisdiction, with well-preserved French administrative records defining its boundaries.
